rows.quote: The town is Kiruna, in the far north of Sweden, above the Arctic Circle.
rows.statement: Kiruna is a town in Norrbotten County in the far north of Sweden, located north of the Arctic Circle.

nguon.title: Station Kiruna Flygplats (lufttemperatur), metadata toạ độ

rows.quote: Under the hill next door is an iron mine, and it is slowly swallowing the ground the old centre stood on. So the town is packing up and moving east.
rows.statement: LKAB's underground iron ore mine in Kiirunavaara, next to Kiruna, causes ground deformation that spreads toward the town, so Kiruna's old centre is being dismantled and the centre relocated about 3 km to the east.

nguon.title: Continued mining affects more of Kiruna

Responsible community development – Annual and Sustainability Report 2025

rows.quote: Houses, shops, a clock tower, even a big red wooden church.
rows.statement: Kiruna's urban transformation involves replacing or moving homes and shops, moving the old town hall's clock tower to the new centre, and moving the large red wooden Kiruna Church (moved in August 2025).

nguon.title: The Bell Tower – Kristallen & Kin Museum

rows.quote: In seventeen thirty-six, a Sámi man named Amund Amundson Mangi reported the iron ore here to the Swedish state. He got a reward, and no taxes for life.
rows.statement: According to LKAB's company history, in 1736 a Sámi man named Amund Amundson Mangi reported the iron ore deposits in the Kiruna area to the Swedish state, and was rewarded with money and exemption from taxes for life.

rows.quote: The town didn't start until nineteen hundred.
rows.statement: Kiruna counts 1900 as its founding year, the year the King approved its town plan.

rows.quote: The mine blasts every night, between one fifteen and one forty-five. The blasting area is cleared first, and the tunnels are aired out for a few hours afterwards. Up on the surface, the ground sometimes shivers.
rows.statement: LKAB's Kiruna mine carries out its production blasting every night between 01:15 and 01:45; the blasting area is evacuated beforehand, the mine is ventilated for a few hours afterwards, and vibrations can sometimes be felt above ground.

rows.quote: According to LKAB, the state-owned company that runs it, this is the world's largest underground iron ore mine.
rows.statement: LKAB, the Swedish state-owned mining company that operates the Kiruna mine, describes it as the world's largest underground iron ore mine (a description from LKAB itself, not independently confirmed).

nguon.title: Kiruna: mining and critical minerals for the future

rows.quote: Its main haulage level sits about one thousand three hundred and sixty-five metres down. That's nearly four and a half thousand feet.
rows.statement: The current main haulage level of LKAB's Kiruna mine is at a depth of 1,365 metres (about 4,480 feet).

nguon.title: The future of sublevel caving is being assessed
LKAB investigates deeper mining operations – pre-feasibility studies for new main haulage levels underway

rows.quote: They take the ore out from below, level by level, and let the rock above cave in behind them. Think of an hourglass. Pull sand from the bottom, and the top of the pile slowly sinks.
rows.statement: LKAB mines Kiruna by sublevel caving: ore is extracted level by level from below and the overlying rock caves in behind the mining, so the ground surface above gradually subsides.

nguon.title: Measures for safer and more efficient mining

rows.quote: And the ore body keeps running east, under the town.
rows.statement: The Kiruna ore body continues eastward beneath the old town (and northward), so ground deformation from mining continues to spread toward the town.

rows.quote: In May twenty twenty, the mine set off the biggest mining-induced earthquake ever recorded in Sweden. Magnitude four point one. Nobody was hurt.
rows.statement: On 18 May 2020 a magnitude 4.1 (ML, Swedish National Seismic Network) seismic event occurred at LKAB's Kiruna mine, the largest mining-induced earthquake recorded in Sweden; no one among the people in the mine was injured.

rows.quote: In twenty twenty-four, Kiruna had a record year, with more than six hundred thousand commercial guest nights.
rows.statement: Kiruna recorded 607,818 commercial guest nights in 2024, a record for the municipality.

rows.quote: My second guess was the hotel made of ice, in the village of Jukkasjärvi, about seventeen kilometres away. That's roughly eleven miles.
rows.statement: Icehotel is located in the village of Jukkasjärvi, about 17 km (about 11 miles) from Kiruna.

nguon.title: Swedish Lapland Jukkasjärvi & What to Expect

rows.quote: Icehotel began in nineteen eighty-nine as an art gallery made of ice and snow.
rows.statement: Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi began in 1989 as an art gallery built of ice and snow (the Arctic Hall), 89 years after Kiruna's founding year of 1900.

rows.quote: Up to sixty-eight wagons, about seven hundred and fifty metres long. Roughly seven football pitches of iron.
rows.statement: Iron ore trains on the Malmbanan line between Kiruna and Narvik run with up to 68 wagons and are about 750 m long, roughly the length of seven 105-metre football pitches.

rows.quote: That sea freezes over every winter.
rows.statement: The sea off Luleå, Sweden's ore port on the northern Gulf of Bothnia east of Kiruna, freezes over every winter.

rows.quote: So they ran a railway the other way, over the mountains, to Narvik on the Norwegian coast. Warm water from the Gulf Stream keeps Narvik's harbour ice-free all year.
rows.statement: The ore railway from Kiruna was built west over the mountains to the port of Narvik on the Norwegian coast, which LKAB says stays ice-free all year thanks to the warm Gulf Stream.

nguon.title: Narvik: our gateway to the world
Narvik: our gateway to the world

rows.quote: The line reached Kiruna around nineteen hundred and was joined up to Narvik in nineteen oh two. The king opened it officially in nineteen oh three.
rows.statement: The railway reached Kiruna around 1900, the line to Narvik was completed in 1902, and it was officially inaugurated by King Oscar II in 1903.

rows.quote: Today, about twelve loaded trains a day still run from Kiruna to Narvik. Luleå ships ore too, with icebreakers helping in winter.
rows.statement: According to Trafikverket, about 12 loaded ore trains a day run from Kiruna to Narvik; Luleå remains an LKAB ore port, and winter shipping there relies on icebreaker assistance.

rows.quote: Kiruna counts nineteen hundred as its birth year, when the king approved its town plan.
rows.statement: Kiruna considers 1900 its year of birth, when the King approved the town plan.

rows.quote: The mining company's first managing director, a geologist called Hjalmar Lundbohm, wanted a model town. He brought in a leading planner to fit the streets to the climate.
rows.statement: Hjalmar Lundbohm, a geologist who became LKAB's first managing director, wanted Kiruna to be a model community and engaged a leading town planner (Per-Olov Hallman) to design a plan adapted to the climate.

rows.quote: By nineteen ten, about seven thousand five hundred people lived here.
rows.statement: Kiruna had about 7,500 inhabitants in 1910.

rows.quote: At the end of twenty twenty-five, the municipality had about twenty-two thousand four hundred. They're spread over an area about the size of New Jersey.
rows.statement: Kiruna Municipality had about 22,400 inhabitants at the end of 2025 (Statistics Sweden) and covers roughly 19,000–19,500 km², about the size of the US state of New Jersey (land area about 19,050 km²).

rows.quote: LKAB says it produces more than eighty percent of the iron ore mined in the European Union.
rows.statement: LKAB states that it produces more than 80 percent of the iron ore mined in the European Union (86 percent in 2025, per its annual report).

rows.quote: Kiruna Church is big, red and wooden, finished in nineteen twelve, and much loved.
rows.statement: Kiruna Church is a large red wooden church completed in 1912 and is one of the town's best-loved buildings.

rows.quote: So on the nineteenth and twentieth of August, twenty twenty-five, it rolled about five kilometres to the new centre, in one piece. It rode on remote-controlled trailers with more than two hundred wheels.
rows.statement: On 19 and 20 August 2025 Kiruna Church was moved in one piece about 5 km to the new city centre on remote-controlled self-propelled trailers with more than 200 wheels.

rows.statement: At its new site Kiruna Church was rotated 180 degrees, so that its front still faces the town.

rows.quote: The parish hopes to reopen it in twenty twenty-seven.
rows.statement: As of November 2026 Kiruna Church remains closed after the move; the Church of Sweden's Kiruna parish hopes to reopen it in 2027.

rows.quote: Eight days after the church parked, LKAB presented a new forecast. About six thousand more people and around two thousand seven hundred more homes would have to move, over roughly the next ten years.
rows.statement: On 28 August 2025, eight days after Kiruna Church reached its new site on 20 August, LKAB presented a new ground-deformation forecast under which about 6,000 more people and about 2,700 more homes in Kiruna would be affected and need to be compensated over the next ten years.

rows.statement: Kiruna homeowners affected by the mine can choose an equivalent replacement home built by LKAB or a payment of the market value plus 25 percent, assessed by an independent certified valuer.

rows.statement: Kiruna's new city centre lies about 3 km east of the old centre.

rows.statement: In Kiruna the polar night, when the sun does not rise above the horizon, lasts from about 11 December to 1 January, roughly three weeks (exact dates vary by a day or two with terrain).

rows.statement: Kiruna's average January temperature is about minus 11 °C (−11.3 °C, about 12 °F) according to SMHI's 1991–2020 normals for Kiruna Airport.

rows.quote: According to a University of Gothenburg study, winter temperatures there can be noticeably lower than at the old site.
rows.statement: A University of Gothenburg study (Jennie Sjöholm, 2025) found that winter temperatures in Kiruna's new centre can be noticeably lower than at the old centre, because it lies in a hollow where cold air collects and its narrow streets and tall buildings block the low winter sun.

rows.statement: Kiruna's North Sámi name is Giron, from the mountain Gironvárri (Kiirunavaara); giron means rock ptarmigan, a bird whose plumage turns white in winter.

rows.statement: In Kiruna the midnight sun lasts from about late May to mid-July, roughly seven weeks, during which the sun does not set.

rows.statement: Most buildings in Kiruna's old centre are demolished and replaced rather than moved, and many residents are unhappy at losing the streets they grew up in.

rows.statement: Gabna, a Sámi reindeer herding community (sameby) near Kiruna, moves its reindeer between summer and winter pastures through the area north of the town; its former route along Lake Luossajärvi was blocked by the mine and the town, and the herds now pass behind the mountain Luossavaara.

rows.quote: It is rich in phosphorus, and in older furnaces that made the iron brittle. In the eighteen-seventies, a new method, the Thomas process, turned that flaw into a selling point.
rows.statement: The Kiruna-area iron ore is rich in phosphorus, which made iron brittle in older production processes; after the Thomas process was invented in the 1870s, phosphorus-rich ore became valuable, one reason the Swedish ore fields became profitable to mine.
